plain_en: Increases digestive fire - improves appetite and the body's ability to digest food.
Helps digest food and undigested toxins (ama) without directly increasing appetite.
Undigested or half-digested material that forms when digestion is weak; considered a root of many diseases.
The liquid or food taken with or after a medicine (e.g. warm water or honey) to help it act and reach the right tissues.
The prescribed time of taking a medicine - before food or after food or at bedtime etc. - chosen by the Vaidya for its effect.
Taken shortly before a meal - often chosen for disorders of the lower body or to act with digestion.
Taken after a meal - often chosen for disorders of the upper body or to reduce irritation to the stomach.
Taken on an empty stomach - usually early morning - for a stronger action; only as the Vaidya advises.
Taken at night before sleep.
Warm water used as anupana - commonly to support digestion and reduce Kapha and Vata.
Honey used as anupana - commonly for Kapha conditions. Never heat honey.
Clarified butter used as anupana or base - nourishing and Vata-Pitta pacifying.
A fine powder of one or more herbs.
A pill or tablet form of an Ayurvedic medicine.
A decoction made by boiling herbs in water and reducing it.
Self-fermented liquid preparations; contain a small amount of natural alcohol.
Ghee processed with herbs.
Medicated oil - for external application or internal use as advised.
A semi-solid jam-like preparation.
Calcined mineral or metal preparation - use only under a qualified Vaidya.
Rejuvenative therapy that supports tissues - immunity and longevity.
Wholesome diet and habits recommended alongside treatment.
Foods and habits to avoid during treatment.
The dosha of movement - dry - cold - light - mobile.
The dosha of transformation - hot - sharp - liquid.
The dosha of structure - heavy - cold - stable - unctuous.
Vata - Pitta and Kapha - the three bodily doshas.
Pacifying treatment with medicines and diet - without purification.
Purification therapy (Panchakarma) - only under supervision.
